sources.entry: Masaka for Codex - Local macOS and Linux CLI that keeps each ChatGPT account and workspace in an isolated CODEX_HOME, shows Codex usage windows, and switches future native Codex sessions without copying tokens. #free #opensource

summary.one_liner: A local macOS/Linux CLI manager that keeps multiple ChatGPT account and workspace profiles isolated, each with its own CODEX_HOME, and switches which one the native Codex CLI uses.
summary.what_it_does: Masaka provides an interactive manager (`masaka`) and terminal subcommands to add, renew, delete, and select profiles, where each profile is one (ChatGPT account, workspace) pair with its own isolated CODEX_HOME. Codex itself handles the official browser login, token refresh, and credential file. The `/status` and `/usage` commands show per-profile login state, token activity, 5-hour and weekly quota windows, reset times, and available reset-card counts. A shell integration (`eval "$(masaka shell-init)"`) makes ordinary `codex` commands launch the selected profile. An optional Proxy mode (Apple Silicon macOS, via `/onboarding`) runs a local launchd daemon so `/use` and automatic switching can route the next request of a running client to another account without interrupting in-flight responses. Automatic switching, priority ordering, and proxy on/off are also available.
use_cases: Keep personal and business ChatGPT workspaces signed in at once
Switch between multiple Codex accounts without logging out
Check quota windows and reset times across several ChatGPT accounts
Route Codex requests to whichever account has spare capacity
Renew one Codex login without affecting other profiles
notable: Each profile gets its own isolated CODEX_HOME; the global ~/.codex/auth.json is never copied or replaced
Proxy mode lets /use switch the account for the next request without interrupting in-flight responses
Automatic switching with a 5% five-hour-window threshold and Pro-first priority ordering
Shell integration wraps the real codex binary and blocks codex login/logout overrides
Profile credentials stored with 0700/0600 permissions; deletion moves to a recoverable trash
caveats: Proxy hot switching is only available on Apple Silicon macOS per the README; direct mode is the general path and changes only future Codex processes
Direct mode allows one managed session per profile; Proxy clients must be restarted once after setup and when turning proxy off
Credentials are stored as plain auth.json files by design (no extra encryption layer), so they must be protected like passwords
Not an official OpenAI product; requires an existing official Codex CLI install
keywords: alternative to manual codex logout login
use another account when quota runs out
